Model and notation

Source: vignettes/articles/Model_notation.Rmd
Model_notation.Rmd

This page works through the mathematical model implemented by inst/multirates_positive_s.stan, and lays each quantity next to the R argument, table or column that supplies it. Read this before vignette("Multirates_inference") if you want to know why the input tables are shaped the way they are, rather than just how to build them.

Two epigenetic states, growth and switching

Cells exist in one of two epigenetic states, written - and +. A population’s size in each state is a vector Z(t)=(Z−(t),Z+(t))Z(t) = (Z_-(t), Z_+(t)), and every lineage in the model (the wild-type background, a driver clade, a driver+clade combo, …) is governed by the same linear ODE, just with its own rate parameters:

dZdt=AZ,A=(λ−ω+→−ω−→+λ+) \frac{dZ}{dt} = A\,Z, \qquad A = \begin{pmatrix} \lambda_- & \omega_{+\to-} \\ \omega_{-\to+} & \lambda_+ \end{pmatrix}

  • λ−\lambda_- is the division rate of - cells.
  • λ+=λ−(1+s)\lambda_+ = \lambda_-(1+s) is the division rate of + cells, written relative to λ−\lambda_- via a fitness coefficient ss (so s>0s>0 means + cells divide faster).
  • ω−→+\omega_{-\to+} and ω+→−\omega_{+\to-} are the rates at which cells switch epigenetic state.

Because AA does not depend on tt, the population at any later time is an exact matrix-exponential solution:

Z(t2)=exp⁡(A(t2−t1))Z(t1) Z(t_2) = \exp\!\big(A\,(t_2-t_1)\big)\,Z(t_1)

This is exactly simulate_Z()’s R implementation (via expm::expm()) and the Stan model’s own Z() Stan function - the same equation, evaluated twice.

The groups: wt, drivers, driver-only clades, driver+clade combos

The population is not a single lineage: it is the wild-type background plus any number of sub-lineages, each founded at its own time from a single cell and governed by the ODE above with its own rate parameters.

Group Founded at Growth s Switch rates Confined to one state?
wt (background) tmint_{min} sepis_{epi} ωn,wt,ωp,wt\omega_{n,wt}, \omega_{p,wt} no
clade_wt (wt sub-lineage) tclade≥tmrcat_{clade}\geq tmrca sepis_{epi} (shared with wt) ωn,wt,ωp,wt\omega_{n,wt}, \omega_{p,wt} (shared with wt) no
driver tdriver≥tmrcat_{driver}\geq tmrca sdrivers_{driver} (own) ωn,driver,ωp,driver\omega_{n,driver}, \omega_{p,driver} (own) no
driver_n tdrivern≥tmrcat_{driver_n}\geq tmrca sdriverns_{driver_n} (own) none (no switching) yes, - only
driver_p tdriverp≥tmrcat_{driver_p}\geq tmrca sdriverps_{driver_p} (own) none (no switching) yes, + only
dc driver leg tdc,1=tmrca+δt,1t_{dc,1} = tmrca+\delta_{t,1} sdcs_{dc} (own) ωn,dc,ωp,dc\omega_{n,dc}, \omega_{p,dc} (own) no
dc clade leg tdc,2=tdc,1+δt,2t_{dc,2} = t_{dc,1}+\delta_{t,2} sdcs_{dc} (shared with its driver leg) ωn,dc,ωp,dc\omega_{n,dc}, \omega_{p,dc} (shared) no

driver_n/driver_p are the simplest case: with no switching, the ODE collapses to plain exponential growth, Z(t)=exp⁡(λ−(1+s)(t−tdriver))Z(t) = \exp\big(\lambda_-(1+s)\,(t-t_{driver})\big). A dc (driver+clade) entity is a nested pair: its driver leg is founded first with a single cell, and its clade leg is a further sub-lineage founded later within the driver leg, sharing the same growth/switch rates - modelling a clade defined by a further epimutation switch event that occurred after the driver mutation.

At each sampling time, the total population in each state is the sum of the wt background and every additive group (driver, driver_n, driver_p, and the dc driver leg - clade_wt and the dc clade leg are nested inside their parent lineage’s mass, not counted again):

Z−tot(t)=Zwt,−(t)+∑iZdriveri,−(t)+∑iZdriver_ni(t)+∑iZdci,−(t) Z^{tot}_-(t) = Z_{wt,-}(t) + \sum_i Z_{driver_i,-}(t) + \sum_i Z_{driver\_n_i}(t) + \sum_i Z_{dc_i,-}(t)

and analogously for Z+tot(t)Z^{tot}_+(t).

The observation model

Cancer cell fractions (CCF) and mutation-arm fractions

A group’s CCF at a sampling time and epistate is simply its share of the total population in that epistate, CCFg(t)=Zg(t)/Ztot(t)CCF_g(t) = Z_g(t)/Z^{tot}(t). This is observed (as data) or predicted (as a posterior draw) with Beta noise of concentration κ\kappa:

CCFgobs∼Beta(CCFg⋅κ,(1−CCFg)⋅κ) CCF_g^{obs} \sim \text{Beta}\big(CCF_g \cdot \kappa,\ (1-CCF_g)\cdot\kappa\big)

kappa is the same idea as bayesplot’s neff_ratio - it controls how tightly the observed fraction is expected to hug its predicted mean; high κ\kappa means a very peaked, low-noise likelihood (see vignette("Convergence_diagnostics") for why a very high kappa can make Stan’s sampler harder to initialize).

Population sizes

Total population sizes in each state at sampling times (zminus, zplus) and at any additional intermediate times (ztot) are observed with lognormal noise of scale σcount\sigma_{count}:

zobs(t)∼LogNormal(log⁡z(t),σcount) z^{obs}(t) \sim \text{LogNormal}\big(\log z(t),\ \sigma_{count}\big)

Mutation counts

Every branch event (the trunk, a driver acquisition, a clade split, …) accumulates mutations as a Poisson process while cells divide. For a branch with growth rate λ\lambda (its own λ−\lambda_- or λ−(1+s)\lambda_-(1+s) once a fitness effect has taken hold) spanning an elapsed time Δt\Delta t:

m∼Poisson(4μℓλΔt) m \sim \text{Poisson}\big(4\,\mu\,\ell\,\lambda\,\Delta t\big)

where μ\mu (mu) is the per-division, per-bp mutation rate and ℓ\ell (l) is the genome length. The trunk uses Δt=tmrca−tmin\Delta t = tmrca - t_{min}; a driver or driver_n acquisition uses Δt=tdriver−tmrca\Delta t = t_{driver}-tmrca; a dc combo’s clade leg uses the post-driver rate λ−(1+sdc)\lambda_-(1+s_{dc}) over Δt=tdc,2−tdc,1\Delta t = t_{dc,2}-t_{dc,1}.

Parameter Prior Set via

sepis_{epi} (s_epi) LogNormal(msepi,σepi)\text{LogNormal}(ms_{epi},\sigma_{epi}) ms_epi, sigma_epi
ωn,wt,ωp,wt\omega_{n,wt},\omega_{p,wt} Gamma(α,β)\text{Gamma}(\alpha,\beta) alpha_n_wt/beta_n_wt, alpha_p_wt/beta_p_wt

sdriveri,sdriver_ni,sdriver_pi,sdcis_{driver_i}, s_{driver\_n_i}, s_{driver\_p_i}, s_{dc_i} LogNormal(ms,σ)\text{LogNormal}(ms,\sigma), one prior per entity ms_driver/sigma_driver columns (etc.) in the entity’s _muts table
ωn,driveri,ωp,driveri\omega_{n,driver_i},\omega_{p,driver_i} (and _dc) Gamma(α,β)\text{Gamma}(\alpha,\beta), one prior per entity alpha_n_driver/beta_n_driver columns (etc.)

Global priors are arguments to fit_multirates(). Per-entity priors (driver/driver_n/driver_p/dc fitness and switch-rate hyperparameters) are supplied per row in the corresponding _muts table, since a well-studied oncogene and a novel candidate driver may legitimately warrant different priors within the same fit.
